One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself. Each time the function calls itself, it breaks the main problem down into a smaller, simpler version of the same task. This repeating process continues until it hits a base case, which is a specific condition that tells the function to stop calling itself. Once the base case is reached, the results from all the smaller tasks are combined and passed back up to provide the final answer.
